channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: UK police detail arrests after far-right rally and counter demo
item.description: Police arrested 12 people in London on Saturday. The arrests followed clashes between a far-right march and counter-protesters. The operation involved thousands of officers. It managed a march by Tommy Robinson's group and a separate anti-fascism rally. The anti-fascism rally also marked Nakba Day. The force had mounted its biggest operation in years to manage both Robinson's "Unite the Kingdom" march and the anti-fascism rally organised by the Stand Up to Racism group combined with protests marking Nakba Day.

item.title: Iran media says ‘no tangible concessions’ in U.S. response to Iran proposal
item.description: Iran's Fars news agency reported Washington offered no tangible The Fars news agency said Washington had presented a five-point list which included a demand for Iran to keep only one nuclear site in operation and transfer its stockpile of highly enriched uranium to the United States.

item.title: India, Netherlands upgrade ties; sign 17 MoUs on water, renewable energy, and semiconductors
item.description: India and the Netherlands elevated their bilateral relationship to a strategic partnership. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Dutch Prime Minister Mark Rutte signed 17 Memoranda of Understanding. These agreements cover water management, renewable energy, and semiconductor manufacturing. TATA Electronics and ASML will collaborate on a semiconductor fabrication project.

item.title: Trump administration promotes program to check voter eligibility; critics fear a midterm purge
item.description: The Trump administration promotes a national program to scan state voter rolls. The scanning of state voter rolls at the national level is part of a broader effort by Republican President Donald Trump to federalise certain election functions and promote his messaging that elections are marred by noncitizen voting, even though instances of that are rare.

item.title: 1.1 billion people live in slums. Can they be housed in dignity?
item.description: Ministers, mayors, and experts are meeting in Baku, Azerbaijan, to Ministers, mayors, international organisations, urban planners and experts are in Baku, Azerbaijan, to tackle one of the world’s fastest-growing challenges: the global housing crisis, which, according to the United Nations, affects nearly 2.8 billion people worldwide.

item.description: Canadian officials confirmed a presumptive hantavirus case in British Columbia. item.title: Donald Trump does ‘not feel optimistic’ for Jimmy Lai after speaking with Xi Jinping
item.description: United States President Donald Trump spoke with Chinese leader Xi Jinping about jailed Hong Kong activist Jimmy Lai. Trump raised Lai's case during their talks. Xi Jinping described the situation as "a tough one." Lai's family had hoped for his release.

item.title: Colorado governor commuted Tina Peters’ sentence after Trump blocked funding for clean water
item.description: Steve Cohen will not seek re-election to the U. S. House of Representatives. Tennessee's Republican-controlled legislature redrew his Memphis-based district. Cohen stated the new map was designed to defeat him. He has represented the ninth congressional district since 2007.

item.title: Trump’s lack of focus on human rights in China is big departure for US diplomacy
item.description: Donald Trump did not raise the case of jailed activist Jimmy Lai with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing. Trump stated he would bring up Lai's case before his departure. He then compared it to asking if he would let former FBI Director James Comey out of jail.

item.title: Mali’s forces target rebel alliance in junta’s fight to keep power
item.description: Mali's armed forces, aided by Russian mercenaries, conducted airstrikes against a coalition of Islamist extremists and Tuareg separatists. This offensive follows an advance by the rebel alliance. The junta is working to retain control amid the ongoing conflict in the west African nation.

item.title: Sudan hunger crisis deepens as UN warns millions face acute food shortages
item.description: The United Nations warned that nearly 20 million people in Sudan face acute hunger. Over 800,000 children risk severe malnutrition this year. Civil war, displacement, and collapsing systems are deepening the humanitarian crisis. Parts of the country are nearing famine conditions.

item.title: As war displaces millions in DR Congo, new schools offer children hope beyond violence
item.description: New schools are opening in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ten-year-old Shadrac Anyazaka does not hesitate when asked about his future. “After finishing my studies, I would like to become President of the Republic one day,” he tells visitors to his school in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

item.title: Somalia at ‘real risk of famine’ as Middle East war fallout continues
item.description: UN aid teams warned Somalia faces a real risk of famine. At least six million people in Somalia are going days without enough food, UN aid teams warned on Friday, highlighting that nearly two million of this number are young children “at high risk of illness or death”.

item.title: Furnace Creek sizzles as snow sweeps Siberia in a week of extremes
item.description: Honduras recorded its all-time May maximum temperature twice this month. Record heat in North and Central America coincides with egg-sized hailstones in eastern ChinaExtreme weather across several parts of the world this week has brought record-breaking temperatures to Honduras, North America and Indonesia. item.title: UN pleads for Equatorial Guinea not to send US asylum seekers to their home countries: ‘Their life
item.description: United Nations human rights experts publicly urged Equatorial Guinea to stop returning US deportees. The experts cited reports of political violence, torture, and death faced by individuals sent back to their home countries. Deportees described being held in prison-like conditions.
